userStories.title: API auto-review columns, repo listing and config
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Persist opt-in auto-review settings, expose them on repo records/DTOs, list eligible repos and resolve bounded poller configuration.

**Motivation** — Nothing in koda notices a new PR or a new push today.

**Approach** — `FleetRepo` gains:

| Column | Type | Default |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `autoReview` | `Boolean` | `false` |
| `autoReviewProfiles` | `String[]` | `[]` |
| `autoReviewMaxCostUsd` | `Decimal(10,4)` | `1.0000` |
| `autoReviewEnabledById` | `String?` | null |
| `autoReviewEnabledByType` | `String?` (`USER` or `AGENT`) | null |
| `autoReviewEnabledAt` | `DateTime?` | null |

plus `@@index([autoReview])`.

`FleetRepoDto` gains:
- `autoReview: boolean`;
- `autoReviewProfiles: string[]`;
- `autoReviewMaxCostUsd: string` (4 places, e.g. `1.0000`);
- `autoReviewEnabledById: string | null`;
- `autoReviewEnabledByType: 'USER' | 'AGENT' | null`;
- `autoReviewEnabledAt: string | null` (ISO).

The Prisma repository's shared row mapping (used by `create`, `findById`, `findAnchor`, `findPage` and the new methods) maps `autoReviewMaxCostUsd` to a 4-place string and `autoReviewEnabledByType` to the union.

`FleetRepoRecord` (`fleet/repos/domain/fleet-repo.domain.ts:6`):
- Baseline: 9 fields.
- Target: adds `autoReview: boolean`, `autoReviewProfiles: string[]`, `autoReviewMaxCostUsd: string`, `autoReviewEnabledById: string | null`, `autoReviewEnabledByType: 'USER' | 'AGENT' | null` and `autoReviewEnabledAt: Date | null`.
- `IFleetRepoRepository.create` keeps its input free of these six fields, and the database defaults fill them.

`FleetReposService.listAutoReviewRepos(50)`: repos with `autoReview` true, provider `github`, a non-null `githubInstallationId` and a project with `deletedAt` null, ordered by `id`, at most 50. The service delegates the supplied limit to findAutoReviewPage; the full-page warning belongs to US-009.

Soft-deleted projects are skipped. `FleetJobsService.dispatch` does not check `Project.deletedAt`, so the repo query used by the poller excludes repos whose project is soft-deleted.

Config (`IFleetConfig`; `FleetConfigSchema` in `fleet.config.ts`; `env.validation.ts`):

| Field | Env | Default | Validation |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `prReviewEnabled` | `FLEET_PR_REVIEW_ENABLED` | `true`; `false` (any case) turns it off | `Joi.string().pattern(/^(true|false)$/i)` optional, like the other boolean flags |
| `prReviewPollMs` | `FLEET_PR_REVIEW_POLL_MS` | `300000` | integer 60000..86400000 |
| `prReviewMaxDispatch` | `FLEET_PR_REVIEW_MAX_DISPATCH` | `10` | integer 1..100 |

Global switch defaults on. `FLEET_PR_REVIEW_ENABLED` defaults to `true`, because every repo's `autoReview` defaults to `false`. The timer starts only when `sweepEnabled` is also true. Timer implementation is US-010. Add migration `20261112090000_fleet_auto_review` with matching Prisma schema. Introduce the shared mapping because the current repository returns raw rows. Update the full repoRecord fixture in threads/project-brief.service.spec.ts with false, [], '1.0000' and three nulls; update common/test-helpers/fleet-config.ts with prReviewEnabled false, prReviewPollMs 300000, prReviewMaxDispatch 10. Also add the same six repo defaults to the created() fixture in fleet-repos.service.spec.ts and the mocked repo.create result in approvals/approval-execution.service.spec.ts: the new FleetRepoDto.from decimal/date mapping receives these mocks too. Keep every existing assertion unchanged and leave constructor-parameter additions to US-002. Do not add production fallbacks for incomplete test records. Extend existing fleet.config.spec.ts, env.validation.spec.ts and repo service unit specs, with real repository round-trips in test/integration/fleet/fleet-repo-auto-review.integration.spec.ts.

**Scope** — In: schema/migration, read mapping/DTOs, eligible page query/delegation and config. Out: configuration writes and DTO validation (US-002), route/catalog/generation (US-003), review-head ledger (US-005), pass/module/poller (US-009/010).

userStories.title: API auto-review settings rules
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add validated, transactional auto-review configuration with requester attribution and project dispatch authorization.

**Motivation** — `FleetRepo` has no review settings.

**Approach** — `PATCH /fleet/repos/:id/auto-review` takes the body `UpdateAutoReviewDto`: `{ enabled: boolean; profiles?: string[]; maxCostUsd?: number }`.
- `profiles` uses the `DispatchFleetJobDto.profiles` decorators: an array of at most 8 strings, each at most 64 characters.
- `maxCostUsd` is a number from 0.0001 to 10000 with at most 4 decimals.

The DTO validates both fields whatever `enabled` is.

`FleetReposService.configureAutoReview(principal: UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal, id: string, dto: UpdateAutoReviewDto): Promise<FleetRepoDto>` maps `principal.actorType` `'user'` to `USER` and `'agent'` to `AGENT`, then applies the rules in this order:

1. An unknown id throws `NotFoundAppException({}, 'fleet.repos')` (404).
2. With `enabled: true`, each of these throws `AutoReviewException(<reason>)` (422, key `fleet.autoReview`):
   - a repo that is not `github`, or that has no `githubInstallationId`: reason `github app required`;
   - a profile that does not match `PROFILE_NAME_RE` or that starts with `RESERVED_PROFILE_PREFIX`: reason `profiles`;
   - duplicate profiles: reason `duplicate profile`;
   - a caller for whom `PermissionService.canHoldKey(<caller ref>, 'fleet.job.dispatch', { projectId: repo.projectId })` is false: reason `caller cannot dispatch in this project`.
3. `enabled: true` sets:
   - `autoReview` to true;
   - `profiles` and `maxCostUsd` when given. An omitted field keeps its stored value, and `profiles: []` stores `[]`;
   - `autoReviewEnabledById` and `autoReviewEnabledByType` to the caller;
   - `autoReviewEnabledAt` to now, only when `autoReview` was false before. Re-saving an enabled repo keeps the original time.
4. `enabled: false` sets `autoReview` false and the three `autoReviewEnabled*` columns to null. It ignores `profiles` and `maxCostUsd` and keeps the stored values.
5. It records the audit entry and returns the repo's `FleetRepoDto`.

The read, the update and the audit run in one `txManager.run`.

`FleetReposService` gains `PermissionService` as a new last constructor parameter (`PermissionsModule` is global).

`IFleetRepoRepository` adds:
- `updateAutoReview(id: string, patch: AutoReviewPatch): Promise<FleetRepoRecord>`, where `AutoReviewPatch` is a partial of the six fields.

Add `AutoReviewException` with {reason}, HTTP 422 and key fleet.autoReview, following RepoCheckException; add en message `Auto-review cannot be configured: {reason}.` and a zh translation carrying {reason}. Persist cost as Decimal and read it through US-001's four-place mapping. Append a PermissionService stub to every direct FleetReposService construction in fleet-repos.service.spec.ts and approvals/approval-execution.service.spec.ts; no existing assertions change. Cover service rules with fleet-repos.auto-review.spec.ts and DTO boundaries without needing a database.

**Scope** — In: DTO/exception/i18n, repository update patch and service transaction/permission/audit behavior. Out: route gate, route variants and catalog/generation (US-003), automatic CAS turn-off (US-005), timer-driven dispatch (US-006 onward). A PATCH that turns auto-review off while a pass is running; that pass can still dispatch reviews for the repo.

**Interface** — `FleetReposService.configureAutoReview(principal: UserPrincipal | AgentPrincipal, id: string, dto: UpdateAutoReviewDto): Promise<FleetRepoDto>`; `updateAutoReview(id: string, patch: AutoReviewPatch): Promise<FleetRepoRecord>`; `{ enabled: boolean; profiles?: string[]; maxCostUsd?: number }`.

userStories.title: API auto-review route and permission key
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Expose auto-review settings through a globally permissioned, approval-gated PATCH and regenerate the API/CLI contract.

**Motivation** — Part A (merged as #360) lets a person dispatch a `REVIEW` job by hand through `POST /projects/:slug/fleet/jobs` with `command: 'REVIEW'` and a `prNumber`.

**Approach** — The controller method is `FleetReposController.configureAutoReview(id, dto)`. It follows the `check` route:
- `@Patch(':id/auto-review')`, `@HttpCode(200)`, `@UseGuards(RequiresGuard)`, `@Requires('fleet.repo.review.configure')`, `@ApprovalGated()`;
- `@ApiOperation({ summary: 'Configure auto-review for a registered repo (fleet.repo.review.configure, global)' })`, `@ApiResponse` entries for 200 (`FleetRepoDto`), 403, 404 and 422;
- `routeGate.run({ key: 'fleet.repo.review.configure', variant: FLEET_REPO_ROUTE_VARIANTS.autoReview, projectId: null, input: { id, patch: dto } })`.

The variant is `rest:fleet-repos.auto-review`. Its route command parses `{ id, patch }` like the role update command (`permission-route.commands.ts:63-66`): the non-empty string `id`, plus `parseBody(UpdateAutoReviewDto, patch)`. It runs `configureAutoReview(principal, input.id, input.patch)` with the principal the loader rebuilds, so a deferred approval records the original requester as the enabler.

userStories.title: API open-PR listing through the App
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add one-page authenticated GitHub open-PR listing with strict provider response mapping and observable fake-forge queries.

**Motivation** — `GitHubAppClient` can read one PR (`getPullRequest`) but cannot list a repo's open PRs.

**Approach** — `OpenPullRequest` (exported from `fleet/git-broker/github-app-client.ts`) has the shape `{ number: number; headSha: string; draft: boolean; headRepoFullName: string | null; updatedAt: Date }`.

`GitHubAppClient.listOpenPullRequests(token, owner, name): Promise<OpenPullRequest[]>` sends `GET /repos/{owner}/{name}/pulls?state=open&per_page=100` through `FleetHttpClient`, one page only.
- It maps each item from `number`, `head.sha`, `draft`, `head.repo?.full_name ?? null` and `updated_at`.
- A reply of exactly 100 items logs a warning, through a Nest `Logger` named `GitHubAppClient`, naming `<owner>/<name>`: PRs past the first page are not seen.
- A non-200 reply throws `RepoCheckException('provider_error')`, like `getPullRequest`.
- These replies also throw `RepoCheckException('provider_error')`:
  - a body that is not an array;
  - an item without a numeric `number`, a string `head.sha`, a boolean `draft` or a string `updated_at`.

Token. Listing PRs needs the Pull requests permission. `mintReadOnlyToken` grants only `contents: read` and `metadata: read`, so the poller uses `mintInstallationToken`, as `FleetPrStateRefresher` does. This story accepts the token; the pass mints it in US-009. Keep the existing Bearer headers and encoded repo path patterns and never log tokens or provider bodies.

`FakeRequest` (`apps/api/test/helpers/fake-forge.ts`): adds `query: string` (the raw query string, `''` when absent). Set it where the path is split from the URL; additive, no existing request field changes. Expand github-app-client.spec.ts against startFakeForge for exact method/path/query/header, mapping, errors and full-page warning.

**Scope** — In: exported OpenPullRequest type, GitHubAppClient method/logger and additive fake-forge query field. Out: head selection (US-006), access recheck (US-008), token mint/orchestration (US-009). Open PRs beyond the first page of 100 per repo per pass; a full page logs a warning. Live verification against GitHub; it needs a nax with the `bot-forge-identity` feature on a runner and happens at deploy.

**Interface** — `GitHubAppClient.listOpenPullRequests(token, owner, name): Promise<OpenPullRequest[]>`; `{ number: number; headSha: string; draft: boolean; headRepoFullName: string | null; updatedAt: Date }`; `FakeRequest.query: string`.

userStories.title: API review-head dispatcher, selection and recovery
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Select eligible PR heads, claim each durably, recover stale pending claims and dispatch bounded REVIEW jobs.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") wants koda to review PRs as they change without anyone dispatching.

**Approach** — What a pass reviews. For each enabled repo, the poller reads one page of up to 100 open PRs and skips a PR that:
- is a draft;
- has a `headRepoFullName` that is null or is not `<owner>/<name>` (compared case-insensitively), meaning it comes from a fork or a deleted repository;
- was last updated before auto-review was turned on (`updatedAt < autoReviewEnabledAt`). When `autoReviewEnabledAt` is null, this rule skips nothing.
The last rule stops the first pass after enabling from reviewing every old open PR at once.

Crash recovery. A `pending` row older than one poll interval (`createdAt < now - prReviewPollMs`) is left over from a pass that stopped between insert and dispatch. The next pass deletes it and handles the head as new.

`ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo(repo: FleetRepoRecord, prs: readonly OpenPullRequest[], opts: { now: Date; pollMs: number; remaining: number }): Promise<number>` handles one repo. It returns the number of `dispatch` calls it made. It walks `prs` in ascending `number`, and for each PR:

1. Skip it under the call-5 rules.
2. Read `findHead`.
   - A `dispatched` or `failed:` row: skip.
   - A `pending` row with `createdAt >= now - pollMs`: skip.
   - An older `pending` row: `remove` it and go on.
3. Stop when the number of calls made has reached `opts.remaining`.
4. `insertPending`. On null, skip.
5. Call `FleetJobsService.dispatch` with:
   - `actorId` = `repo.autoReviewEnabledById` and the repo's `projectId`;
   - the body `{ command: 'REVIEW', repoId, prNumber, profiles: repo.autoReviewProfiles, maxCostUsd: Number(repo.autoReviewMaxCostUsd) }`;
   - opts `{ auditKey: 'system.pr-review.dispatch' }`.
   On success, `markDispatched` with the result's job id. On a throw, apply call 7.

Every `FleetPrReview` write runs in `bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...)`.

Per-pass cap on attempts. A pass makes at most `prReviewMaxDispatch` (default 10) `dispatch` calls, across all repos, whether they succeed or fail. Heads it did not reach are picked up by a later pass. This also bounds the load while a budget is paused. The dispatcher enforces its remaining argument; cross-repo accounting belongs to US-009. Call 7's failure outcomes land in US-007, not this story. The pass provides the system/onBehalfOf context in US-009; do not invent an unregistered system writer here. Use result.job.id, not a top-level id. Avoid an open transaction around FleetJobsService.dispatch. Add BOOKKEEPING_REASONS entry fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping and matching EXPECTED_REASON_IDS entry in audit-coverage.bookkeeping.spec.ts; widen FleetJobsService.dispatch opts.auditKey from `'fleet.job.dispatch' | 'thread.plan' | 'thread.run' | 'system.schedule.dispatch'` to include `'system.pr-review.dispatch'`. Unit tests use an in-memory IFleetPrReviewRepository and injected jobs fake, verifying currentBookkeepingReason for every write. Extend the existing apps/api/src/fleet/jobs/fleet-jobs.service.spec.ts with the regression assertion that omitted opts.auditKey still produces fleet.job.dispatch; no new test file is needed for that assertion.

**Scope** — In: selection, sorting, unique claim, fresh/stale pending recovery, successful dispatch/linking, per-call cap and bookkeeping registration. Out: retry/permanent failure mapping (US-007), enabler permission checks (US-008), repo orchestration/writer (US-009) and timer (US-010). Re-reviewing a head whose `REVIEW` job failed or was cancelled; its row stays `dispatched` until the PR gets a new head. A duplicate review when the API stops after `dispatch` commits and before `markDispatched`; the `pending` row is replaced after one poll interval and the head is dispatched again. Reviewing draft PRs and PRs from forks. Reviewing a head whose PR was last updated before auto-review was turned on. Recording which head a `REVIEW` job actually reviewed; nax reviews the PR's current head when the job runs, so a head that arrives while a review is queued can be reviewed twice.

**Interface** — `ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo(repo: FleetRepoRecord, prs: readonly OpenPullRequest[], opts: { now: Date; pollMs: number; remaining: number }): Promise<number>`.

userStories.title: API review-head dispatcher, failure outcomes
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Classify dispatch failures into retryable removal, permanent failed outcomes and budget-paused repo termination.

**Motivation** — The fleet design (§9.122, "S6 = K1 + K2") wants koda to review PRs as they change without anyone dispatching.

**Approach** — Retry later, not never. A dispatch that fails for a reason that can clear later deletes the head's row, so a later pass tries the head again:
- `BudgetPausedException` (`fleet.budgetPaused`). Every PR of the repo shares the project's budget, so the dispatcher also stops the rest of that repo's PRs for this pass.
- `ConflictAppException` with key `fleet.jobs` (409): a `REVIEW` for the PR is still active. This happens when a new head arrives while the last review runs.
- Any other unexpected error. It is also logged at warn level with the repo id, the PR number and the error name.
The exceptions are checked in that order, because `BudgetPausedException` is a `ConflictAppException`.
A dispatch that fails for a reason a retry cannot fix keeps the row as `failed:<reason>`:
- `ValidationAppException`: its `args.reason` when that is a string, else the class name;
- `NotFoundAppException` or `FleetDispatchException`: the class name.
The stored outcome is cut to 200 characters.

`ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo(repo: FleetRepoRecord, prs: readonly OpenPullRequest[], opts: { now: Date; pollMs: number; remaining: number }): Promise<number>` continues to return the number of dispatch calls including throws. Every `FleetPrReview` write runs in `bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...)`. Wrap both remove and markFailed paths; never make dispatch itself bookkeeping. Use a Nest Logger on the dispatcher and log only error names plus repo id/PR number for unexpected failures, not token/provider payloads. A fleet.jobs conflict does not stop subsequent PRs; a budget pause does. Store the truncated whole string including failed: prefix. Do not copy ScheduleTicker's unexpected-error active-job recovery: even an unexpected post-commit dispatch error removes this head's row. Cover these outcomes through an in-memory ledger and typed exception instances in review-head-dispatcher.outcomes.spec.ts; selection behavior from US-006 stays unchanged.

**Scope** — In: dispatch throw classification, failed outcome truncation, retry cleanup, warning and per-repo budget stop. Out: core PR selection/claim algorithm (US-006), permission gate (US-008), cross-repo pass cap/module (US-009). An unexpected error thrown after `dispatch` has committed the job (placement, live publish or ticket effects) removes the head's row; later passes then get 409 until that job ends and review the head again. Suppressing failure notifications for poller-dispatched reviews; a failed review notifies its user requester like any job, and agent requesters get none, as today.

**Interface** — `ReviewHeadDispatcher.dispatchRepo(repo: FleetRepoRecord, prs: readonly OpenPullRequest[], opts: { now: Date; pollMs: number; remaining: number }): Promise<number>`; permanent outcome `failed:<reason>`; retryable outcome deletes the row.

userStories.title: API enabler gate
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Revalidate the stored user or agent's project dispatch permission and automatically disable stale access before polling.

**Motivation** — Nothing in koda notices a new PR or a new push today.

**Approach** — Re-check every pass. Before polling a repo, the poller checks the enabler with the schedule rule, `mayDispatch(access, keys)` (`fleet/schedules/schedule-access.ts:12`):
- `access` comes from `IFleetPrReviewRepository.findPrincipalAccess(enabler)`. A USER exists when its `User` row does and is disabled when `User.disabled` is true. An AGENT exists when its `Agent` row does and is never disabled.
- `keys` is `PermissionService.effectiveKeys(enabler, { projectId: repo.projectId })`.
The check lives in `EnablerGate.check(repo): Promise<PrincipalRef | null>`. It returns the enabler when the check passes. On a failed check it calls `FleetReposService.disableAutoReview(repo.id, 'enabler_lost_access', enabler.id)` and returns null, and the pass does not dispatch for that repo.

Compare-and-set turn-off. `disableAutoReview(id, reason, expectedEnablerId)` changes the row only when `autoReview` is true and `autoReviewEnabledById` equals `expectedEnablerId`. It records its audit entry only when it changed the row, and returns whether it did. So a pass reading a stale repo list cannot turn off a repo someone else has just re-enabled.

Build the PrincipalRef from the repo's stored autoReviewEnabledByType/id, not a currently signed-in human or approver. Reuse mayDispatch directly; do not duplicate key semantics, consult agent liveness or substitute a global scope. Await automatic disable, then return null even if its CAS returned false. Read, effectiveKeys and disable errors propagate for US-009's repo-local catch and warning. This class performs no token/PR reads or direct job dispatch. Unit-test it with an in-memory IFleetPrReviewRepository, PermissionService stub and FleetReposService.disableAutoReview stub in reviews/enabler-gate.spec.ts. The pass later places the gate inside onBehalfOf context so the disable audit carries the enabler.

**Scope** — In: stored principal reconstruction, principal/access/key recheck, mayDispatch reuse and failed-gate CAS disable call. Out: database access lookup/CAS implementation (US-005), runAsSystem/writer/module (US-009), dispatcher (US-006/007) and poller (US-010).

**Interface** — `EnablerGate.check(repo): Promise<PrincipalRef | null>`; `findPrincipalAccess(ref: PrincipalRef): Promise<{ exists: boolean; disabled: boolean }>`; `PermissionService.effectiveKeys(enabler, { projectId: repo.projectId })`.

userStories.title: API PR review pass and module
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Boot a registered system writer that polls eligible repos under their enablers' identities and enforces a shared dispatch-attempt cap.

**Motivation** — No component dispatches `REVIEW` jobs.

**Approach** — Polling, not a webhook. The `koda-fleet` App is installed with no webhooks and the reference deployment listens on loopback only, so GitHub cannot call koda. The poller reads through the App, like `FleetPrStateRefresher`.

The enabler is the requester. Turning auto-review on stores the caller's principal (`type` and `id`) and needs the caller to hold `fleet.job.dispatch` in the repo's project at that moment. The poller dispatches each review with `actorId` = the enabler's id inside `runAsSystem('pr-review', ..., { onBehalfOf: enabler })`, the `ScheduleTicker` shape, so the job's `requestedByType` is the enabler's type.

`FleetPrReviewPass` has `@SystemWriter('system.pr-review.dispatch')` and is the system writer for this feature. `FleetPrReviewPass.run(now): Promise<void>` runs its whole body inside `runAsSystemWriter(this, ...)`.

`FleetPrReviewPass.run(now)`:

1. Reads `FleetReposService.listAutoReviewRepos(50)`: repos with `autoReview` true, provider `github`, a non-null `githubInstallationId` and a project with `deletedAt` null, ordered by `id`, at most 50. A full page logs a warning.
2. For each repo, with `remaining = prReviewMaxDispatch - calls made so far`:
   1. Inside `runAsSystem('pr-review', ..., { onBehalfOf: <the stored enabler> })`, so the turn-off audit and the dispatch audit both carry the enabler:
   2. Call `EnablerGate.check(repo)`. On null, go to the next repo.
   3. Mint a token with `mintInstallationToken(installationId, name)` and read `listOpenPullRequests(token, owner, name)`.
   4. Run `dispatchRepo(repo, prs, { now, pollMs: prReviewPollMs, remaining })`.
3. A throw anywhere in step 2 for one repo is logged at warn level with the repo id and the error name, and the pass goes on to the next repo.
4. The pass ends when `remaining` reaches 0.

Token. Listing PRs needs the Pull requests permission. `mintReadOnlyToken` grants only `contents: read` and `metadata: read`, so the poller uses `mintInstallationToken`, as `FleetPrStateRefresher` does.

Audit.
- The settings change records audit key `fleet.repo.review.configure`.
- The poller's writes to `FleetPrReview` run inside `bookkeeping('fleet.pr-review-bookkeeping', ...)`.
- Each dispatch records audit key `system.pr-review.dispatch` through `FleetJobsService.dispatch`.
- An automatic turn-off records audit key `system.pr-review.dispatch`.

The pass, the poller, `EnablerGate` and `ReviewHeadDispatcher` live in a new `FleetReviewsModule` (`apps/api/src/fleet/reviews/`), which `FleetModule` imports.
- It provides them plus `PrismaFleetPrReviewRepository` and `FLEET_PR_REVIEW_REPOSITORY`.
- `PrismaFleetPrReviewRepository.findPrincipalAccess` reads the `User` and `Agent` tables directly, as `PrismaScheduleRepository.findOwnerAccess` does; this is the accepted precedent, not a layering breach.
- It imports `FleetReposModule`, `FleetJobsModule` and `GitBrokerModule`, and exports nothing.
- `FleetReposModule` adds `FleetReposService` to its `exports`, so the poller can inject it. The repository token stays where it is.

This story registers the pass, gate, dispatcher and repository; US-010 adds the poller provider when its lifecycle class is authored. Add the system catalog key `system.pr-review.dispatch` (inventory row and `INVENTORY_SCOPE_ROWS`, system access). Add `'system.pr-review.dispatch': ['system']` right after `'system.schedule.dispatch'`. The system key, its writer class and that class's module registration land together in US-009, because the permission contract checks every catalog key against the writers of the booted module. Add TSV system row for FleetPrReviewPass (run by FleetPrReviewPoller on a setInterval), mirroring ScheduleTicker columns. Update system-writer.decorator.spec.ts writers map with FleetPrReviewPass/key and exact count 34->35. Update role-matrix.spec.ts exact cells 220->221; in each role snapshot add system.pr-review.dispatch after system.schedule.dispatch as non-role-key, non-role-key, leaving every other entry identical. System actor ids derive from catalog keys, so no separate hardcoded actor allowlist is needed.

Use unit tests stubbing listAutoReviewRepos/listOpenPullRequests/EnablerGate/dispatcher and inspecting action context. A DB-free FleetReviewsModule compilation test mocks external PrismaService, TRANSACTION_MANAGER, config, permission and other imported collaborators through providers. Include all per-repo failure sources: mint, list, enabler check and failed automatic turn-off. Errors in the initial repo list can escape run for US-010 to log.

**Scope** — In: pass orchestration, enabler context, shared cap, containment/warnings, system catalog/TSV/snapshot changes and module registration/export. Out: timer/single-flight ownership (US-010), settings route (US-003), selection/outcomes (US-006/007) and permission gate internals (US-008). More than 50 auto-review repos per pass; repos past the first 50 by id are not polled, and a full page logs a warning. Fair sharing of the per-pass cap between repos; repos are polled in id order, so a low-id repo with many retrying heads can use the whole cap. A narrower PR-read token; the poller uses the installation token that `FleetPrStateRefresher` uses. A GitHub webhook trigger for reviews; reviews are found by polling through the App.

userStories.title: API PR review poller lifecycle
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Schedule review passes through an opt-out, single-flight lifecycle component that never rejects from poll().

**Motivation** — Nothing in koda notices a new PR or a new push today.

**Approach** — `FleetPrReviewPoller` owns the lifecycle:
- On `onModuleInit`, when `sweepEnabled` and `prReviewEnabled` are both true, it starts an unref'd `setInterval` of `prReviewPollMs` that calls `poll()`.
- `onModuleDestroy` clears the interval.
- `poll()` calls `FleetPrReviewPass.run(new Date())` once. A `poll()` that starts while an earlier one is unresolved returns without calling `run`. `poll()` never rejects; an error escaping `run` is logged at error level by the poller's Nest `Logger`.

Global switch defaults on. `FLEET_PR_REVIEW_ENABLED` defaults to `true`, because every repo's `autoReview` defaults to `false`. The timer starts only when `sweepEnabled` is also true.

Add FleetPrReviewPoller to the existing FleetReviewsModule providers. Keep runAsSystemWriter/@SystemWriter on FleetPrReviewPass (US-009), not on a second writer class. Use finally to release single-flight state on success and failure, clear/null timer on destroy, and avoid a startup pass not requested by the spec. Unit tests use fake timers and a deferred pass promise to assert callback timing, unref/cleanup, both enable gates and overlap; extend the existing DB-free fleet-reviews.module.spec.ts to resolve the poller.

**Scope** — In: poller class/provider, timer, shutdown, single-flight and top-level error logging. Out: pass/repo loop/system writer/catalog (US-009), head dispatch policy (US-006/007), config defaults/validation (US-001).

**Interface** — `FleetPrReviewPoller.poll(): Promise<void>`; `onModuleInit`; `onModuleDestroy`; `FleetPrReviewPass.run(now): Promise<void>`.

userStories.description:
**Goal** — Let permitted global administrators enable, edit or disable a repo's auto-review settings without misrepresenting pending approvals.

**Motivation** — `FleetRepo` has no review settings.

**Approach** — On `/admin/fleet/repos`, each GitHub repo with an App installation gets an auto-review control, the component `FleetRepoAutoReview` (file `components/fleet/RepoAutoReview.vue`, auto-imported by Nuxt under that name). Its switch is enabled only when `useGlobalPermissions()` has `fleet.repo.review.configure`. Turning it on, or choosing the edit button of an enabled repo, opens a dialog with:
- a profiles field (comma-separated);
- a max-cost field;
both validated with vee-validate and zod. Saving calls `useFleetRepos().setAutoReview` with `enabled: true`; turning the switch off calls it with `{ enabled: false }`.

`setAutoReview` returns `{ kind: 'pending', request }` when the API's data has a `permissionKey` (the 202 approval summary), and `{ kind: 'saved', repo }` otherwise. Strings live under `fleet.repos.autoReview.*` in `en` and `zh`.

Web `FleetRepo` (`apps/web/lib/fleet-types.ts:120`) adds the six fields. `useFleetRepos` adds `setAutoReview(id, body): Promise<{ kind: 'saved'; repo: FleetRepo } | { kind: 'pending'; request: ApprovalRequestSummary }>`.

The API fields are autoReview boolean, autoReviewProfiles string[], autoReviewMaxCostUsd four-place string, autoReviewEnabledById string|null, autoReviewEnabledByType 'USER'|'AGENT'|null and autoReviewEnabledAt ISO string|null. PATCH body is `{ enabled: boolean; profiles?: string[]; maxCostUsd?: number }`; profiles accepts at most 8 strings, each at most 64 characters; max cost is 0.0001..10000 with at most 4 decimals. Use existing API wrapper/apiPath and extractApiError. Read the permission composable's computed permission set rather than roles. Keep the switch controlled by persisted repo state: opening the enabling dialog is not a save; 202 keeps old state and shows fleet.repos.autoReview.pending; a saved response updates the displayed repo. Choosing edit pre-fills the stored chain/cost; split and trim comma-separated profiles, sending numeric cost. A 422 shows the API message from extractApiError. Localize every label, validation error, action and pending notice in both JSON locales; use the existing Switch/dialog/input primitives and HSL design tokens. Preserve explicit-only forge checks and all existing repo actions.

Extend tests/helpers/mount-sfc.ts FleetComponentName and FLEET_COMPONENT_FILES with FleetRepoAutoReview mapped to RepoAutoReview.vue, so pages mount the real component; no other entry changes. Add only a Switch stub to tests/helpers/fleet-harness.ts uiStubs. In tests/pages/admin-fleet-repos.spec.ts, mountRepos supplies a useGlobalPermissions stub granting fleet.repo.review.configure unless overridden and includes FleetRepoAutoReview in fleetComponents; repo fixtures gain all six fields with autoReview false, empty profiles, '1.0000' and three nulls; existing assertions stay unchanged. Add tests/components/repo-auto-review.spec.ts for dialog/permission/API result and error behavior.

**Scope** — In: repo web type/composable PATCH union, per-row control/dialog, permission gating, en/zh strings and mounting integration. Out: API route/settings rules (US-002/003), background polling/dispatch (US-006 through US-010), layout/navigation redesign. Showing a repo's review history (`FleetPrReview` rows) in the web. GitLab auto-review.

**Interface** — `setAutoReview(id, body): Promise<{ kind: 'saved'; repo: FleetRepo } | { kind: 'pending'; request: ApprovalRequestSummary }>`; `FleetRepoAutoReview` at `components/fleet/RepoAutoReview.vue`; API path `/fleet/repos/<id>/auto-review`.

outOfScope: A GitHub webhook trigger for reviews; reviews are found by polling through the App.
Reviewing draft PRs and PRs from forks.
Open PRs beyond the first page of 100 per repo per pass; a full page logs a warning.
More than 50 auto-review repos per pass; repos past the first 50 by id are not polled, and a full page logs a warning.
Reviewing a head whose PR was last updated before auto-review was turned on.
Recording which head a `REVIEW` job actually reviewed; nax reviews the PR's current head when the job runs, so a head that arrives while a review is queued can be reviewed twice.
Re-reviewing a head whose `REVIEW` job failed or was cancelled; its row stays `dispatched` until the PR gets a new head.
A duplicate review when the API stops after `dispatch` commits and before `markDispatched`; the `pending` row is replaced after one poll interval and the head is dispatched again.
A PATCH that turns auto-review off while a pass is running; that pass can still dispatch reviews for the repo.
Suppressing failure notifications for poller-dispatched reviews; a failed review notifies its user requester like any job, and agent requesters get none, as today.
Deleting old `FleetPrReview` rows; they are kept.

An unexpected error thrown after `dispatch` has committed the job (placement, live publish or ticket effects) removes the head's row; later passes then get 409 until that job ends and review the head again.
Fair sharing of the per-pass cap between repos; repos are polled in id order, so a low-id repo with many retrying heads can use the whole cap.
A `fleet.repo.check` approval requested before an auto-review change and approved after it answers 409 `fleet.repos`, because `prepareCheck` compares the whole repo row; this is accepted.
